title: What If the World's Rice Harvest Failed for a Year?

scenes.text: What if the world's rice harvest failed for a year? Half of humanity would feel it.
Rice is the staple food for over half the world's people and supplies about 20 percent of all calories.
World stocks, a record 198 million tonnes, equal about 38 percent of a year's consumption. Roughly four months.
And most of it sits in two countries. India and China hold nearly three quarters.
We have seen the panic early. When India curbed exports in 2023, global rice prices hit a 15-year high.
In the 2008 rice crisis, about 100 million people were put at risk. A full failure would dwarf it.

description:
What if the world's rice harvest failed for a year?
Stocks would cover only about four months, and even a single export ban in 2023 pushed prices to a 15-year high.
